correctness.rationale: All shortest-path distances are verified directly; the zero-sum vector space has an exact orthogonal three-eigenspace decomposition that diagonalizes the powered distance matrix, so the normalized sharp Rayleigh gap and all equality cases are algebraic. The scalar threshold has a unique root from strict monotonicity of \((2^p-1)/3^p\) for \(0\le p\le1\); all exponents above one fail by convexity. Schoenberg double-centering gives exact endpoint rank and dimension; an independent Taylor expansion proves the quantified biclique comparison. Exact rational and floating checker evaluations use the bundled program, without treating finite tests as infinite proof. Limit: independent audit has not been performed.

originality.rationale: The connected crown graph has a three-distance metric not covered by the two-distance split-graph and clique-bouquet classifications. The inspected primary full-text sections give general negative-type criteria and complete-bipartite formulas, or different four-point roundness results, not the stated \(n\)-parameter crown classification. Targeted searches found no equivalent formula. The general spectral criterion permits computation for individual finite metrics but does not imply the explicit all-parameter equation, sharp gap, rank jumps, and matching-deletion comparison without the new decomposition. Full Deza–Maehara and Matoušek texts remain a specifically identified limitation, not a claim of exhaustive literature coverage.
residual_risks: An implicit complete crown-graph formula in Deza–Maehara (1990) or other unavailable full text cannot be excluded.
Matoušek (1996) was not directly available in full; a related isometric snowflake statement might be overlooked.
Historical/semantic research search may miss differently phrased stronger results.

value.rationale: The crown graphs are a canonical distance-transitive family obtained by deleting a perfect matching from the complete biclique. The result determines the exact generalized roundness, a sharp attained normalized gap and critical Euclidean embedding dimension for all connected members, finds the first loss of \(1\)-negative type at ten vertices, and gives a counterintuitive strict improvement over the biclique baseline with second-order asymptotics. These are natural complete-family metric invariants, not arbitrary selected test cases. Risk: structural elegance alone does not guarantee historical originality, already limited in the originality assessment.
